topic: Claude Sonnet 4 Developer Guide: API, Features & Benchmarks (2026)

key_points: Launch source for Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4, positioning Sonnet 4 as a major upgrade over Sonnet 3.7 for coding, reasoning, and instruction following.
Highlights Claude 4-era capabilities: extended thinking with tool use, parallel tool execution, memory improvements, better instruction following, and fewer shortcut/loophole behaviors.
Gives the original Claude Sonnet 4 SWE-bench Verified headline result of 72.7%, useful as the historical baseline for the guide.
Official API reference for current model IDs, pricing, context windows, output limits, knowledge cutoffs, and provider IDs.
As of June 2026, the current Sonnet 4-family API model is claude-sonnet-4-6, with 1M context, 64K max output, extended thinking, adaptive thinking, and $3 input / $15 output per million tokens.
Explains that Claude 4.6 generation model IDs are dateless but pinned snapshots, not evergreen aliases.
Developer walkthrough aimed at API beginners, covering account setup, SDK calls, Python and JavaScript examples, code execution, and model comparison.
Uses the original claude-sonnet-4-20250514 model ID, which creates an opportunity to update the article with 2026 guidance for claude-sonnet-4-6.
Frames Sonnet 4 as the balanced production model for everyday development and coding workloads.
Competitor guide focused on the original Claude 4 launch, model specs, pricing, API features, migration notes, and benchmark interpretation.
Lists original Sonnet 4 specs: 200K context, 64K max output, $3 input / $15 output per million tokens, and March 2025 knowledge cutoff.
Notes API features such as parallel tool execution, extended thinking with tool use, memory improvements, and reduced shortcut behavior.
Covers newer Sonnet 4.6 access, features, and benchmarks from a developer education angle.
Emphasizes API access via model ID claude-sonnet-4-6 and unchanged Sonnet pricing of $3 input / $15 output per million tokens.
Highlights 1M context, adaptive thinking, context compaction, computer use, and improved tool integration as the 2026 differentiators.

stats.fact: Original Claude Sonnet 4 scored 72.7% on SWE-bench Verified at launch, edging Claude Opus 4's 72.5% launch figure while targeting a more cost-efficient production tier.

Claude Sonnet 4.6 is the current Sonnet 4-family model in Anthropic's 2026 model table, with API ID claude-sonnet-4-6, $3 per million input tokens, $15 per million output tokens, 1M-token context, 64K max synchronous output, extended thinking, and adaptive thinking.

Anthropic's Sonnet product page says Sonnet 4.6 is available through the Claude Platform, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry; the 1M-token context window is API-only beta on that page.
Anthropic states Sonnet 4.6 pricing remains $3 input / $15 output per million tokens, with prompt caching offering up to 90% savings and batch processing offering 50% savings.

The official SWE-bench site defines SWE-bench Verified as a human-filtered subset of 500 real-world software engineering tasks, so benchmark claims should specify the scaffold and date rather than being treated as universal coding accuracy.

Prompt caching is designed to resume from repeated prompt prefixes and reduce latency and cost for repeated context, making it especially relevant for codebase agents, RAG systems, and long shared system prompts.
Claude tool use lets the model return structured tool calls that the application executes for client tools, while Anthropic executes server tools; tool definitions count toward input tokens.
Extended thinking with tool use in Claude 4 models supports interleaved thinking, allowing the model to reason between tool calls after receiving intermediate results.
Batch processing is documented as a way to process asynchronous jobs and can be paired with longer prompt-cache durations when many batch requests share context.
Web search tool support gives Claude access to real-time web content and returns citations, useful for apps that need answers beyond a model's knowledge cutoff.

angles: Lead with a 2026 update note: developers searching for Claude Sonnet 4 often need both the original claude-sonnet-4-20250514 context and the current claude-sonnet-4-6 API guidance.
Position Sonnet as the default balanced API model: strong enough for agents and coding, cheaper than Opus, and materially more capable than older Sonnet 3.7-era workflows.
Make model IDs a practical pitfall section: old dated IDs, current dateless pinned IDs, Bedrock IDs, Vertex AI IDs, and why aliases should be controlled in production.
Separate benchmark marketing from production evaluation: explain SWE-bench Verified, scaffold sensitivity, cost, latency, max output, and tool reliability.
Show cost architecture patterns: prompt caching for repeated codebase context, Batch API for offline work, Haiku for classification, Sonnet for agent loops, Opus for hardest planning.

Build a developer checklist around API features that matter in production: streaming, tool use, extended thinking, citations, file/search inputs, rate limits, retries, observability, and data retention.
Use a migration angle: what changes when moving from Sonnet 3.7 or original Sonnet 4 to Sonnet 4.6, including context window, output limits, model ID naming, and adaptive thinking.
Include vendor/platform guidance: direct Anthropic API versus Bedrock, Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry, and what enterprise buyers trade off in routing, data residency, and operational controls.
